name: Spellbreak
audience: time-blind workdays, ADHD hyperfocus, and long coding tunnels on a Mac
problem: time disappears in a tunnel, corner banners lose to deep focus within days, and a break you can dismiss with a reflex never happens
promise: The screen goes quiet and changes colour for the length of the break, then hands the screen back. No account, no streak to protect, nothing leaving the Mac.
differentiators: Lock mode takes the skip ring away. The break runs its clock.
One purchase. No subscription, no account, no streak to keep.
The app has no network access at all — sandboxed, sealed, notarized.
Apple silicon and Intel, macOS 13 and later.

notes:
MONETISATION, because the fleet is not uniform and copying the wrong shape is the fastest way to sound fake. Spellbreak is a ONE-TIME APP SALE: the buyer pays A$29 and owns the notarized DMG, unlocked, forever. It is NOT a supporter pass, NOT a yearly membership, NOT a free tier with an upsell. ZipList and TalkType in the same fleet sell $29/year supporter passes and their copy reads like a membership; Hexbloop sells its app once, like Spellbreak. Never import pass language (tiers, membership, supporter, unlock more lists) into this kit. The Mac App Store lane (free + 7-day trial + US$9.99) is PARKED and must not appear in any copy: today there is one price and one way to buy.
One maker, Melbourne. The voice observes and never instructs — no "you", no questions, no imperatives beyond a control's own label. Lock mode is the only thing that may be called unskippable; the default break is left with a brief hold, on purpose. Never quote a hold longer than 3 seconds or a break longer than 3 minutes.
